name: Impressionism — Light & Color
summary: Plein-air light study: cream canvas, five low-saturation pastels behaving like mixed pigment, broken brushstroke rules, dissolved edges, and a soft dappled-light overlay drifting across a strict underlying grid.
whenToUse: When the user asks for Impressionism, Monet/Renoir light and color, a plein-air or painterly aesthetic, soft pastel dapple, broken brushstrokes, gallery-calm fine-art atmosphere, or a romantic garden-light interface that still has to stay readable and well-gridded.

effects.dapple: radial-gradient(circle at 18% 22%, rgba(246,231,178,.55) 0 14px, transparent 15px), radial-gradient(circle at 46% 38%, rgba(246,231,178,.38) 0 22px, transparent 23px), radial-gradient(circle at 72% 14%, rgba(163,201,168,.22) 0 18px, transparent 19px), radial-gradient(circle at 88% 56%, rgba(246,231,178,.30) 0 12px, transparent 13px), radial-gradient(circle at 34% 76%, rgba(184,167,214,.20) 0 20px, transparent 21px)

rules: Paint in layers, not in fills: every panel is a 2–3 stop gradient of near-neighbour pastels (background → surface → the lightest wash) so the surface looks brushed rather than vector-flat, and no large area is ever one solid hex.

Dapple before you decorate: the sun-dappled light layer is this mode's signature — one warm sunlight ellipse from the upper left plus broken circles of #f6e7b2, #a3c9a8, and #b8a7d6 at 20–40% alpha drifting across it, applied as an overlay at mix-blend-mode: soft-light, never as a repeating hard pattern and never on top of small text.

Break the stroke: dividers, underlines, and selected-state markers are short dashes (10–18px on, 6–10px off) or a hand-wobbled 2px rule at 40–70% opacity — no full-width 1px hairline ever runs edge to edge.

Keep the palette in the light: sky #a8d0e6, blush #f6c6c0, leaf #a3c9a8, lavender #b8a7d6, and sunlight #f6e7b2 on a cream #f7f2e6 canvas, with ink #3a3a3a reserved for text and thin accents. Every hue stays under roughly 35% saturation and none of them glow.

Text goes in ink, color goes behind it: pastels are fills, washes, borders, and daubs only — any label sitting on a pastel is #3a3a3a, and any pastel used as text must be the deep ramp (#7fa8c9, #7fa885, #8f7cb5) at 18px bold or larger.

Set type quiet and generous: Cormorant or Playfair Display at 500–600 for headings from 28px up with 1.15 line-height and Title Case — never all caps, never wide tracking — EB Garamond 400 at 17–19px/1.65 for body, and IBM Plex Mono at 13px with 0.02em tracking for data only.

Edges dissolve, they never blur: 10px radius on cards, 16px on media, full pills on buttons, and where a panel must fade into the canvas use a gradient or mask-image dissolve over 24–40px — never backdrop-filter, glass, or a Gaussian halo.

Move like weather: 240–420ms on cubic-bezier(.4,.14,.3,1) ease-out only; hover lifts 2px and warms 3–5% in brightness, focus breathes the sunlight glow in and out once, and nothing springs, bounces, blinks, or slides further than 4px.

Leave the brushmarks visible: let the dapple overlay, broken rules, and gradient banding cross component boundaries so the page reads as one painted surface — while the layout grid underneath stays strict, because the softness is in the pigment, never in the alignment.

copywriting.voice: A painter thinking out loud at the easel: unhurried, concrete, sensory, quietly delighted. Copy names the light and the color before it names the action ('The light is moving — 400 saved strokes.'), prefers one clean clause to three modifiers, and never sells, never jokes at the reader's expense, and never raises its voice. Instructions stay plain and short so the poetry lives in the framing, not in the labels.

case.commands: sentence case imperative ('Begin the study', 'Pin it to the wall')

avoid: deadpan system errors ('Invalid input.', 'An error occurred')
stacked exclamation marks, all-caps sentences, and loud urgency ('Hurry!', 'Last chance!')
emoji, mascots, and playful arrows used as bullets
art-historical jargon in user-facing labels ('impasto', 'scumbling', 'en plein air' as a button)
any artist signature, artwork title, or painted image reproduced or imitated

do: Build every large surface from two or three near-neighbour pastels in a gentle gradient, and let the dapple overlay fall across panels, headers, and empty space so the light looks like it is on one continuous canvas.
Use the five pastels for fills, washes, borders, and daubs — and put all text in ink #3a3a3a, or in a deep ramp hue at 18px bold and up when color is unavoidable.
Break every rule you draw: dashes of 10–18px, a wobbled 2px underline, an 8px daub instead of a bullet; nothing should look like a vector hairline pulled end to end.
Dissolve edges with a 24–40px gradient or mask rather than blurring them, so softness reads as paint meeting canvas instead of a photographic depth of field.
Set headings in Cormorant or Playfair Display 500–600 Title Case from 28px up with 1.15 line-height, body in EB Garamond 400 at 17–19px/1.65, and keep IBM Plex Mono to 13px data only.
Animate like shifting light: 240–420ms ease-out, a 2px lift on hover, a warmth or brightness shift of a few percent, one breathing glow on focus — then rest.
Draw decorative daubs from primitives (soft blob, broken dash, radial dapple, vignette wash) rather than shipping any painting, poster, or museum image.
dont: No artworks, reproductions, crops, textures sampled from paintings, artist signatures, or museum wall labels — evocation comes from palette, edge, and light only.
No neon, no high-saturation accent above roughly 35% saturation, no pure white cards, and no pure black text — the darkest value in the system is ink #3a3a3a.
No hard offset shadows, no glow rings, no glassmorphism or backdrop-blur, and no more than one soft warm shadow per component.
No 0-radius rectangles, no 1px full-width hairlines, and no crisp geometric dividers — a hard edge stops the surface reading as painted.
No all-caps headings, no wide letter-spacing on display type, no script or handwriting fonts, and no mono type in running paragraphs.
No springy or bouncy easing, no loops, no parallax that moves more than a few pixels, and no animation longer than 900ms.
No saturated red error states, no color-only status (always add the word), and no small pastel text — it will fail contrast on cream every time.
accessibility: Ink #3a3a3a on canvas #f7f2e6 clears AAA for body text, but sky #a8d0e6, blush #f6c6c0, leaf #a3c9a8, lavender #b8a7d6, and sunlight #f6e7b2 all fail as small text on cream — use them as fills and borders with ink on top, or step down to the deep ramp (#7fa8c9, #7fa885, #8f7cb5) at 18px semibold or larger.

Danger #b5546a on cream sits near 4.3:1: keep error copy at 16px bold or larger, always pair the hue with the words and a visible border change rather than a red fill alone, and never communicate state by color only.

Cormorant and Playfair Display are light-coloured at small sizes: hold display at 28px and up with weight 500 or higher, keep body at 17px/1.65 minimum, avoid long strings of italic, and never place body copy directly over the dapple overlay without raising the panel background toward #fdfaf2.
Honor prefers-reduced-motion: stop the dapple drift, the hover lift, and the focus breathing, and swap them for instant brightness or border changes so nothing moves but state stays fully legible.

Give every focusable element a visible 2px ink #3a3a3a focus ring with 3px offset, since pastel-on-pastel bounds are too low-contrast to act as a focus indicator on their own; keep the dapple overlay pointer-events: none so it never intercepts input.
Keep body measure between 60 and 72 characters and paragraph spacing at 1.2em so the soft palette and generous leading never force a reader to re-find their place.
signatureElement: Sun-dappled light: broken brushstroke bands of sky, blush, leaf, lavender, and sunlight layered over a cream canvas, crossed by a soft warm dapple overlay that drifts like light through leaves — with every edge dissolved and every rule left visibly brushy

prose.overview: This mode paints the interface as a sunlit plein-air study: a warm cream canvas, five low-saturation pastels that behave like mixed pigment, and a dappled light overlay that falls across the whole page as if through moving leaves. Nothing is outlined hard or filled flat — panels are built from two or three near-neighbours of one hue, edges dissolve over 24–40px, and rules break into short brushstrokes instead of drawing hairlines. The result should read as one painted surface with a strict grid underneath: the softness lives in color, edge, and light, never in sloppy alignment. It is calm, airy, and quietly romantic — a morning in a garden rather than a museum wall.
prose.colors: The canvas is warm cream #f7f2e6 with panels a shade lighter at #fdfaf2, and ink #3a3a3a carries every piece of text plus the thinnest edges. Five pastels do the painting: sky #a8d0e6 for primary action and water-cool calm, blush #f6c6c0 for warm accents and selected states, leaf #a3c9a8 for success and growing things, lavender #b8a7d6 for secondary accents and quiet highlights, and sunlight #f6e7b2 for the dapple, focus warmth, and warning. No area is one solid hex — every large surface is a two- or three-stop gradient of near-neighbours, so the color shifts the way wet pigment does. Each hue carries a light/base/dark ramp, and only the deep ramp is allowed to become text, because a pastel on cream will always lose the contrast fight.
prose.typography: Cormorant leads at 500–600 for headings from 28px up, with Playfair Display and EB Garamond as the graceful fallbacks; its high-contrast strokes and open apertures set the period tone, so a geometric or grotesque face is never a substitute. Body copy is EB Garamond 400 at 17–19px with 1.65 line-height and a measure of 60–72 characters, which gives the text the unhurried pace the palette promises. Headings are Title Case and never tracked out — letter-spacing on a serif this fine simply looks broken — and italics are used for asides, captions, and placeholders. IBM Plex Mono appears only at 13px for data: dimensions, revisions, timings, coordinates, the small instrument readings that let a painting be a working surface.
prose.layout: Layout is an easel composition on a strict 12-column grid: a 4px spacing scale stepping 4/8/16/24/40px, wide 40px margins, and generous vertical air so no panel touches another. Blocks are allowed to sit asymmetrically the way a composition does — a wide panel with a small note card floating to one side — but every edge snaps to the grid and every column stays true. Readers move left to right through a study: subject, then detail, then the small caption underneath the way a title card hangs below a canvas. Softness is spent on edges, gradients, and the dapple overlay; it is never an excuse to nudge a box, and 24px gaps never become 22px because it looked nicer.
prose.elevation: Depth is light, not shadow: a single wide, warm, low-opacity shadow (0 18px 40px -24px rgba(127,168,201,.45)) lifts a panel a few millimetres off the canvas, and a soft 0 6px 14px -10px contact shadow holds small controls down when pressed. Internal depth is a sunlight glaze — inset 0 0 32px rgba(246,231,178,.35) — which reads as warm light pooling inside a frame rather than as a bevel. Nothing casts a hard offset, nothing glows neon, and where a surface must recede it fades into the canvas through a gradient or mask-image dissolve instead of blurring. Layers stack like glazes: each one is thinner and more transparent than the one beneath, and none of them is glass.
prose.shapes: Everything is soft-edged: 10px radius on cards, inputs, and menu rows, 16px on media and large washes, full pills on buttons, and a deliberately uneven blob radius (48% 52% 55% 45% / 52% 46% 54% 48%) for decorative daubs and the toggle knob. Rules break into 10–18px dashes with 6–10px gaps, or wobble as a 2px underline, so no line runs as a clean hairline from edge to edge. Shapes are simple — soft rectangle, soft pill, soft circle — with interest coming from color shift and dapple rather than from ornament, bevels, or geometric flourishes. Perfect squares, 0-radius cards, and hard 1px boxes have no place on a painted surface.
prose.components: Panels are cream gradients with a 1px ink-alpha edge, a 10px radius, one warm outer shadow, an inner sunlight glaze, and a dapple overlay at 55% in soft-light; headings inside get a broken blush underline. Buttons are pills painted with a sky-to-sunlight gradient and ink labels, which lift 2px and warm on hover, settle on press, and show a 2px ink focus ring instead of a bright outline. Inputs are near-white wells with an inset cool wash that turns warm and rings softly in sky on focus, and errors switch the border to a muted rose with an italic sentence rather than a saturated red. The status bar is a studio note — italic Garamond on the left, 13px mono data on the right, pastel daubs marking saved, still wet, and failed — and the toggle is a sun dial whose cream blob knob travels across a cool-to-warm track in 240ms. Menus are quiet lists where the selected row is a sunlight wash with a dashed blush brushstroke down its left edge, never a solid bar.
prose.dosDonts: Do build surfaces from layered pastels, do let the dapple fall across component boundaries, do break every rule into brushstrokes, do keep ink text on pastel fills, and do let motion feel like light shifting rather than elements sliding. Don't reproduce any painting, detail, signature, or museum image, don't push a hue past roughly 35% saturation, don't reach for hard offsets, glass, or neon, and don't trade a strict grid for a painterly look — the calm only works when the arrangement is exact.
